newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rabin's granddaughter says every day a nightmare.
newsitem.headline: Rabin's granddaughter says every day a nightmare.

text.p: The granddaughter of slain Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin said on Wednesday life had been a nightmare since he was assassinated by a religous Jew nearly a year ago.
Noa Ben-Artzi, whose eulogy moved world leaders to tears at Rabin's funeral, spoke to Israel Television as Israel prepared to mark the anniversary of the assassination.
"I don't remember much from those days...it's been one long nightmare since then," said Ben-Artzi.

"Everything that happened after the murder, if it was strange or ugly or painful, it doesn't resemble the things that happened before. My world is divided into two and if you ask me, it's clear that I would like to live in the old one," she said.
Yigal Amir shot Rabin dead at a Tel Aviv peace rally on November 4 to stop his government from handing over control of parts of the West Bank to the Palestinians.

Rabin's 1993 handshake with PLO leader Yasser Arafat on the White House lawn signalled an historic conciliation with the Palestinians but transformed Rabin into a traitor in the eyes of some right-wing Jews.
Israel marks the assassination on Thursday, the anniversary according to the Jewish calendar.

"I part from you, hero, rest in peace and think and miss us because we down here love you very much. And may the heavenly angels, I ask them, accompanying you now, take good care of you because you deserve their protection," Ben-Artzi said at Rabin's funeral last year, attended by dozens of world leaders.
